title: The eve
hook: both armies camped; the conch shells; Arjuna's hands shake
carry: the gita begins with arjuna's despair

segments.voice: Yesterday: needle's point, the land Duryodhana wouldn't give. Even Krishna asked for peace first.

The night before something big. The exam, the surgery, the wedding, all playing in your head while you lie awake. A wide plain in north India, called Kurukshetra. Two vast armies camped on it, the story says: kings from every corner of the land, elephants, chariots, horses, foot soldiers stretching to the horizon. Tomorrow cousins fight cousins. Far away in the palace, the blind king Dhritarashtra can't see any of it. So he asks his charioteer, Sanjaya, who has been given the gift of seeing the battlefield from afar, to tell him what's happening.
screen: `THE NIGHT BEFORE.` → `KURUKSHETRA: TWO ARMIES.` → `THE BLIND KING ASKS.`

segments.voice: His question is the very first line of the Bhagavad Gita. In Sanskrit it begins: dharmakshetre kurukshetre samaveta yuyutsavah. On the field of dharma, the field of the Kurus, gathered, eager to fight: what did my sons and the sons of Pandu do? Notice what he calls it: not just a battlefield, a field of dharma. Sanjaya tells him. The grandfather Bhishma, commander of the Kaurava army, blows his conch shell, a sound like a lion's roar. The other side answers. Krishna, who has agreed to drive Arjuna's chariot, lifts his conch, named Panchajanya. Arjuna blows his, Devadatta, the god-given. Conch after conch, until the sound shakes the sky and the earth. Then Arjuna says to Krishna: drive my chariot out between the two armies; I want to see who I'm fighting. Krishna drives into the empty space in the middle, and Arjuna looks. On the other side he sees his grandfather Bhishma, who raised him. His teacher Drona, who taught him to shoot. His uncles, his cousins, his friends' sons. And the great archer starts to shake. In the Gita's words, as closely as i can put them: his limbs give way, his mouth goes dry, his skin burns, his hair stands on end, and his great bow slips from his hand. He sits down in the chariot. And here's the surprise. Tradition titles this first chapter of the Gita the yoga of Arjuna's despair. Even the breakdown counts as part of the path. Krishna's teaching doesn't begin when Arjuna is brave; it begins when he admits he can't go on.
screen: `ON THE FIELD OF DHARMA.` · `DRIVE ME BETWEEN THE ARMIES.` · `THE BOW SLIPS FROM HIS HAND.` · `CHAPTER ONE: ARJUNA'S DESPAIR.`

segments.voice: Notice your hands, calm or restless, and think of something you're on the eve of: a conversation, a hard day tomorrow. If Arjuna's feeling is there, the dry mouth, the heavy limbs, don't push it away; in the Gita, despair is the first chapter, not the last. If you pray, tell God plainly what you can't do, the way Arjuna told Krishna. Then breathe, slow in, slower out; you don't have to be ready yet.
The eve. Two armies on the field of dharma, the conches sounding, and a great archer with shaking hands.
Your line: the Gita begins with Arjuna's despair. He sits in the chariot, and Krishna is about to speak. That's day seventy-six.

howItsDone: The Bhagavad Gita, which opens on this scene, is recited daily by many Hindus, often chapter by chapter; the conch shell is still blown in temples and homes at the start of worship.

what a scholar hears: dharmakshetre kurukshetre, the field of dharma. the chapter's traditional title is arjuna vishada yoga, the yoga of Arjuna's despair. it sits inside the Mahabharata's Bhishma Parva.
